# Matthew Cuthbert

## Overview

- **Age:** Sixty years old  <sub>[v1 c2 P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v1 c2 P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v1 c37 P5](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0005), [v1 c37 P9](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0009)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v1 c2 P2](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0002)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v1 c2 P0](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

He was an odd-looking personage with an ungainly figure, stooping shoulders, and long iron-gray hair. Ever since he was twenty years old, he wore a full, soft brown beard. When he passed away, his long gray hair framed a placid, smiling face.

_Sources: [v1 c2 P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003), [v1 c37 P11](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0011)_

## Personality

Matthew was an extraordinarily quiet, soft-spoken, and shy man who deeply dreaded strangers and women, fearing they were secretly laughing at him. Despite his extreme reclusiveness, he was exceptionally soft-hearted, generous, and gentle, acting as a quiet champion and confidant for Anne Shirley. He possessed a wordless love for nature and sweet flowers.

_Sources: [v1 c2 P2](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0002), [v1 c2 P3](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0003), [v1 c25 P24](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0024), [v1 c37 P11](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0011)_

## Goals

- To provide a good home and education for Anne Shirley  <sub>[v1 c30 P16](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0016)</sub>

## History

Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables in Avonlea alongside his sister Marilla. Intending to adopt an orphan boy to help with farm work, Matthew drove to Bright River station, where he instead encountered Anne Shirley. Unable to turn her away, he brought her back to Green Gables and convinced Marilla that they should raise and educate her. Over the following years, Matthew served as Anne's quiet advocate and supporter, encouraging her studies for the entrance examination to Queen's Academy. For Christmas one year, despite his terror of shopping and dealing with clerks, he arranged through Mrs. Rachel Lynde to buy Anne a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves. Years later, after returning home from the post office, Matthew collapsed and died instantly at the doorway from the shock of reading a newspaper report detailing the failure of the Abbey Bank.

_Sources: [v1 c2 P0](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0000), [v1 c2 P7](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0007), [v1 c2 P17](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0017), [v1 c25 P9](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0009), [v1 c25 P24](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0024), [v1 c25 P25](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0025), [v1 c30 P14](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0014), [v1 c30 P16](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0016), [v1 c37 P1](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0001), [v1 c37 P9](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0009)_

> I’m not expecting a girl. It’s a boy I’ve come for. He should be here. Mrs. Alexander Spencer was to bring him over from Nova Scotia for me.  <sub>[v1 c2 P7](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0007)</sub>
